source: Massoudi & Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for Conceptual Systems Engineering and Design
finding: A nine-role multi-agent system (MAS) was compared with a two-agent system (2AS) on requirements, functional decomposition and simulator code for a solar water filter. The simple 2AS made code that ran far more often. The MAS covered more requirements and made bigger graphs.
numbers: 60 runs: 2 models (Llama 3.3 70B, DeepSeek R1 70B) x 2 systems x 3 temperatures x 5 seeds. JSON validity 100% everywhere. Requirement coverage peaked at 20% (R1, MAS, T=0). Code executability: R1 2AS T=0 100%; Llama 2AS T=0.5 94.7%; MAS mostly under 50% (Llama MAS 40.2%, R1 MAS 34.8%). Llama MAS completed 0 of 5 runs.
limits: One domain; only 'code executes' checked, not physics; 5 seeds; prompts hand-tuned with o3.
agent_relevance: More roles and more structure did not help. A thin decomposition loop with a code check beat an elaborate one. Supports G7 (the schema must pay for itself) and keeping O3 small.

source: Massoudi & Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for Conceptual Systems Engineering and Design
finding: Decomposition was stored as a Design-State Graph: sub-function node, one embodiment, physics models, linked requirements. Even the best MAS graph (8 subsystem nodes) had physics errors. Flow edges (mass, energy, information) were often declared but not coherently connected.
numbers: Best MAS graph: 8 nodes (power, filtration, pump, storage, control, sensors, UI, housing), scripts over 50 lines. Best 2AS graph: 4 nodes, stubs of 5-15 lines. Errors seen: solar model without panel area; pump with specific gravity instead of density.
limits: Same single case study; no expert rating of decomposition quality.
agent_relevance: Models decompose to plausible-looking parts but get the flows between parts wrong. A check on flow consistency (code, not model) is the missing piece for O3.

source: Massoudi & Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for Conceptual Systems Engineering and Design
finding: Main failure modes were non-termination and context overflow, not wrong content. The loop hit the recursion limit of 30 most often, mainly with Llama.
numbers: Recursion limit 30; 60,000 max completion tokens; Llama MAS 0/5 completions; R1 MAS 2/5; R1 2AS T=0 5/5 in 38.6 s versus about 650 s for MAS.
limits: Limits were chosen by the authors.
agent_relevance: Decomposition loops need a hard budget and a program-owned stop rule (G6 and the program-decides rule in section 1).

source: Elhambakhsh, Grandi & Ko (2025) A Domain Adaptation of LLMs for Classifying Mechanical Assembly Components
finding: Task is the lowest level of function modelling: label which of 8 function classes a part serves. Untuned GPT models were nearly useless. A fine-tuned GPT-3.5 Turbo was very good with little data.
numbers: Test accuracy of base models: GPT-3.5 Turbo 0.04, GPT-4o Mini 0.20, GPT-4 Turbo 0.27. Fine-tuned with 10% of data (681 samples) 0.89 accuracy (macro F1 0.64); with 90% (6,130) 0.63 (macro F1 0.56). OSDR 7,568 unique parts; 6,786 ABC parts labelled, about 99% inside the label set.
limits: Accuracy fell as training data grew (authors guess overfitting and class imbalance: channel and support dominate). No ground truth on ABC. Text says 4% to 90%, table says 0.89.
agent_relevance: Function vocabulary is not in the model by default. A fixed verb-noun vocabulary in the prompt matters for O3. Do not trust fine-tuning curves that fall with more data.

source: Haddad & Seibel (2025) Functional decomposition of technical products based on LLMs and Monte Carlo tree search
finding: MCTS-FD wraps GPT-4o in Monte Carlo tree search to build function structures. Reported better error rate and graph connectivity than smaller models, and compared with graduate student outputs.
numbers: No numbers on the abstract page (full text timed out). Venue ICED 2025, Proc. Design Society vol 5 pp 1913-1922, DOI 10.1017/pds.2025.10205.
limits: Abstract page only; comparison models unnamed; no figures read.
agent_relevance: Search over decompositions with a structural check (connectivity) is a candidate O3 variant. Needs numbers from the full paper before use.

source: Rosenthal, Demke, Mantwill & Niggemann (2023/2024) Plan-Based Derivation of General Functional Structures in Product Design
finding: Functional decomposition is cast as AI planning. The 30 Roth functions become PDDL actions (verb + noun). Input and output flows become start and goal states. A modified partial-order planner (POP) returns the function structure.
numbers: Two worked examples, both solved: coffee maker (start: stored water, electric, powder; goal: hot coffee) and siege engine (start: human power, timber; goal: ram wall). Output is ordered steps with parallel groups, e.g. guide water and guide energy, then convert energy, then add.
limits: Quality judged by experts, no numbers, no runtime, no baseline. Needs start and goal states already written in verb-noun form. Ignores requirements, physics effects and variants. Peer version ICPS 2024.
agent_relevance: The cleanest non-LLM model of decomposition: code searches, a fixed library supplies the parts. This fits the rule that code decides and the model fills slots. Gives O3 a symbolic fallback with checkable preconditions.

source: Rosenthal, Demke, Mantwill & Niggemann (2023/2024) Plan-Based Derivation of General Functional Structures in Product Design
finding: Authors state no earlier work treated general functional decomposition as planning. Older related work reduced circuit design to solver calls (QBF) and mined component-function association rules (Tensa 2019).
numbers: Function library size 30 (Roth). Solutions are partial orders: independent sub-functions may run in any order.
limits: Self-claimed novelty; narrow literature search by the authors.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a preconditions-and-effects check on each sub-function is feasible in code, so G3-style checks can apply to decompositions.

source: Zhou et al. (2022) Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Split the problem into easier sub-problems, solve in order, feed earlier answers forward. On SCAN length generalization it reached at least 99% with 14 examples.
numbers: SCAN: at least 99% any split with 14 exemplars (code-davinci-002); chain-of-thought 16%. Specialised neural-symbolic models were trained on over 15,000 examples.
limits: Abstract page only. SCAN is a synthetic grammar task; GSM8K and DROP numbers not read.
agent_relevance: Strong sign that explicit ordered decomposition fixes length and size generalization. Note the gain is on a task with a clean recursive structure.

source: Khot et al. (2023) Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks
finding: Each sub-task goes to its own prompt, a tool or symbolic code. Beat chain-of-thought and least-to-most on k-th letter concatenation and list reversal at long lengths; beat baselines on CommaQA-E, HotpotQA, MuSiQue.
numbers: Text gave trends only: near 100% on letter concatenation while CoT methods drop with word count; exact values only in figures 7, 8, 10, 12 (not read). Gains on HotpotQA mostly in smaller models; Codex on HotpotQA about equal.
limits: No exact numbers extracted. Models are GPT-3 era.
agent_relevance: Sub-tasks can be replaced by code (counting, retrieval). Matches our rule: put the countable steps in code.

source: Prasad et al. (2023/2024) ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning with LLMs
finding: Decompose only when the executor fails, and do it recursively. Beat ReAct, Plan-and-Execute, Reflexion on three interactive benchmarks with GPT-3.5.
numbers: Success %: ALFWorld ADaPT 71.6 vs ReAct 43.3, Plan-and-Execute 43.3, Reflexion 57.5. WebShop 44.0 vs ReAct 32.0, Plan-and-Execute 17.0, Reflexion 35.0. TextCraft 52.0 vs ReAct 19.0, Plan-and-Execute 27.0, Reflexion 32.0.
limits: Success signal comes from the LLM executor; on WebShop its self-judgement was over 30 points above the real reward, which can stop decomposition too early. d_max=3 or 4.
agent_relevance: Direct support for G1: split only on a failure signal, not on a schedule. Upfront static decomposition (Plan-and-Execute) was the worst on WebShop (17.0 vs 32.0 ReAct).

source: Prasad et al. (2023/2024) ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning with LLMs
finding: Gains are larger the deeper the task. Planner and executor can be different models: a stronger planner lifts a weak executor.
numbers: TextCraft recipe depth 2: ReAct 26.9 vs ADaPT 78.2; depth 3: ReAct 1.8 vs ADaPT 38.7. ALFWorld dev: GPT-3.5 alone 38.4, with GPT-3.5 planner 58.3; LLaMA-2-70B alone 20.4, with GPT-3.5 planner 43.3. WebShop 3 products: 27.5 vs 47.5; 10 products: 20.0 vs 42.5.
limits: Dev sets, single runs; TextCraft is the authors' own dataset.
agent_relevance: Decomposition value rises with compositional depth. Planning can be bought separately from execution.

source: Press et al. (2022/2023) Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
finding: Models often answer every sub-question right yet miss the combined question. That gap stayed near 40% from 1B to 175B parameters, so scale did not fix it.
numbers: Gap roughly constant 40% for GPT-3 sizes; 42.9% for ChatGPT; 23.0% for GPT-4.
limits: Multi-hop trivia, not design. Figure values not read.
agent_relevance: Knowing the parts is not the same as composing them. The composing step is where a program-owned check should sit.

source: Press et al. (2022/2023) Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
finding: Self-ask (model writes and answers follow-up questions) beat chain of thought, and plugging a search engine into the sub-questions beat it further.
numbers: davinci-002 accuracy %: Bamboogle direct 17.6, CoT 46.4, self-ask 57.6, self-ask+search 60.0. 2WikiMultiHopQA exact match: direct 25.4, CoT 29.8, self-ask 30.0, self-ask+search 40.1.
limits: Bamboogle graded by the authors by hand; small sets.
agent_relevance: External answers to sub-questions (tool, retrieval) beat the model answering all alone. Fits operator use of real output (G2).

source: Dziri et al. (2023) Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
finding: On multiplication, logic grids and dynamic programming, errors compound across a computation graph. Models seem to match remembered sub-graphs, not run an algorithm.
numbers: 3-digit x 3-digit multiplication: ChatGPT 55%, GPT-4 59%. For 4x2 digits, 82.3% of final-correct answers still held at least one wrong step in the graph. Propagation errors usually exceeded local errors. Scratchpad fine-tuning failed out of distribution.
limits: Exact per-size accuracies only in plots. Older models.
agent_relevance: A correct final answer can hide wrong sub-steps, so check sub-results, not just the end. Deep decomposition without checks piles up error.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
finding: Failure taxonomy for multi-agent LLM systems built from 150 traces: 14 failure modes in 3 groups (system design, inter-agent misalignment, task verification).
numbers: MAST-Data: over 1,600 annotated traces, 7 frameworks. Annotator agreement kappa 0.88. Models: GPT-4, Claude 3, Qwen2.5, CodeLlama.
limits: Abstract page only: no per-mode percentages read; task-decomposition share unknown.
agent_relevance: Splitting work across roles creates new failure points at the hand-off and at verification. Another reason for one agent with code-owned hand-offs.

source: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems (2025)
finding: Whether splitting work across agents helps depends on how decomposable the task is. It helps when sub-tasks are independent and hurts when steps depend on each other.
numbers: 260 configs, 6 benchmarks, 5 architectures, 3 LLM families. Finance Agent (D=0.41) centralized +80.8% (0.631 vs single 0.349). PlanCraft (D=0.42) every multi-agent variant lost: hybrid -39.1%, centralized -50.3%, independent -70.0% (single 0.568). SWE-bench Verified -2.1% to -14.9% (single 0.522).
limits: Cross-validated R2 only 0.373. SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench use 20-instance subsets. Aggregate multi-agent effect -0.3% with 95% CI about -58.7% to +77.2%. Finance baseline numbers inconsistent across figures.
agent_relevance: Sequential dependence, not task size, decides if a decomposition pays. O3 should first test for independence of the parts and fall back to one thread when the parts chain.

source: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems (2025)
finding: Extra agents stopped paying once a single agent was already decent (about 0.45 raw score). Error amplification was far higher without a central checker.
numbers: Error amplification vs single agent: independent 17.2x, decentralized 7.8x, hybrid 5.1x, centralized 4.4x. But the main effect was not significant after controls (p=0.658). Capability ceiling term beta=-0.236, p=0.004.
limits: Amplification factors are architecture constants applied to all benchmarks; authors say efficiency and overhead explain results better.
agent_relevance: A central code-owned verification step may cut error spread between sub-functions. Weak signal, so test before relying on it.

source: Zelikman et al. (2023) Parsel: Algorithmic Reasoning with Language Models by Composing Decompositions
finding: Parsel writes a hierarchy of function descriptions in plain language, implements each function many ways, and picks combinations that pass tests. It is functional decomposition used inside a code-generation loop.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 85.1% (prior best 67%); up to 8 Parsel programs 91.5% pass@any. At 128 programs: direct 84.1% vs Parsel 93.9%. APPS competition 25.5% vs 14.5% prior. GPT-4 alone vs Parsel: Parsel solved 18 HumanEval tasks GPT-4 missed; GPT-4 solved 2 that Parsel missed.
limits: Prior-art number 67% is not one controlled Codex run. A 2.7B CodeGen solved 0 of 25 APPS problems. Needs tests to pick among implementations.
agent_relevance: Strongest direct match for O3: decompose, implement parts separately, select by running tests. Selection by execution, not opinion (G5, G8).

source: Zelikman et al. (2023) Parsel: Algorithmic Reasoning with Language Models by Composing Decompositions
finding: The decomposition mattered, not just the sampling. Turning the same plans directly into Python lost most of the gain. Human raters preferred Parsel plans in robot planning.
numbers: Direct-to-Python ablation: pass@8x16 6% vs 25.5% full pipeline (100 APPS problems). VirtualHome: Parsel plan judged more accurate in 69% of comparisons. Expert human solved 5 of 10 problems in 6 hours; GPT-3 + Parsel solved 2 of 10.
limits: Small human case study; ablation on 100 problems only.
agent_relevance: Decomposing is not enough alone; the per-part search with checks adds value.

source: Jiang et al. (2023) Self-planning Code Generation with Large Language Models
finding: Model first writes a short step plan, then code step by step. Improves pass@1 over direct and chain-of-thought code generation, and a perfect plan would help far more.
numbers: code-davinci-002 8-shot HumanEval pass@1: direct 48.1, code CoT 53.9, self-planning 60.3, ground-truth plan 74.4. MBPP-sanitized: 49.8, 54.5, 55.7, 65.1. Small models: text-curie 0.0 both, code-cushman-001 34.0 direct vs 30.1 planned.
limits: Gain needs a large model; small models lose or stay flat. Multi-turn plan variant scored 28.2.
agent_relevance: The gap between self-made plan (60.3) and a correct plan (74.4) shows plan quality is the bottleneck. Score the plan with code before spending tokens on it.

source: Radhakrishnan et al. (2023) Question Decomposition Improves the Faithfulness of Model-Generated Reasoning
finding: Answering sub-questions in separate contexts makes the stated reasoning match what the model does more closely, at a small accuracy cost.
numbers: HotpotQA accuracy CoT 87.3 vs factored decomposition 83.0; TruthfulQA 78.7 vs 75.3. Adding-mistakes test: answer changed 9.6% (CoT) vs 33.6% (factored). Suggested-answer bias drop: 21.3% (CoT) vs 9.2% (factored). Base model: same as Claude 1.3.
limits: Four QA tasks only. Early-answering results only in plots.
agent_relevance: A decomposition whose parts really drive the answer is a better record than free-form reasoning (supports section 1 claim that written reasoning is unreliable).

source: Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve Prompting
finding: Zero-shot prompt that asks the model to plan sub-tasks and then carry them out beat zero-shot chain of thought on all ten datasets and matched 8-shot CoT on math.
numbers: 10 datasets, 3 reasoning types, GPT-3. No accuracy figures on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract only; no exact numbers read.
agent_relevance: A one-line plan-then-solve cue is a cheap baseline that any O3 must beat at equal tokens (G7).

source: Cross-reading: Rosenthal 2023 planner vs Massoudi & Fuge 2025 LLM agents
finding: Two ways to automate decomposition now exist: a symbolic planner over a fixed function library, and LLM agents over free text. The planner is correct by construction but needs formal inputs; LLM agents take plain text but give inconsistent flows.
numbers: Planner: 2 worked examples, 30-function library, both solved. LLM agent: requirement coverage at most 20%, executable code 34.8% to 100% depending on setup.
limits: Different tasks and no shared benchmark: no head-to-head. No standard benchmark for function-structure quality was found.
agent_relevance: A hybrid is the open niche: model proposes verb-noun parts in plain text, code checks each part's inputs and outputs with a planner-style check.

source: Cross-study summary of decomposition gains (ADaPT, Self-planning, Parsel, Scaling Agents)
finding: Across 2022-2025 papers, decomposition helps most on deep, compositional tasks where each part can be checked, and helps little or hurts on tightly chained tasks or when the model is already strong.
numbers: ADaPT TextCraft depth 3 1.8% to 38.7%; Parsel HumanEval 67% to 85.1%; self-planning +25.4% rel. over direct on HumanEval; PlanCraft multi-agent -39.1% to -70.0%; SWE-bench -2.1% to -14.9%.
limits: Different models, tasks and baselines; my reading, not one meta-analysis. None of these tests engineering design function structures.
agent_relevance: Rule for O3: use only when sub-parts are separable and checkable; use as-needed (on failure), not by default.

source: Search gap note: LLM tests of Stone and Wood style function structures
finding: Found only three LLM papers aimed at engineering function structures (Massoudi 2025, Haddad 2025, Elhambakhsh 2025) plus the pre-LLM Rosenthal planner. None replicates the Purdue human studies or rates decomposition against the Stone-and-Wood functional basis.
numbers: Counts: 3 LLM design-specific papers found; 0 with a human-vs-model replication; only Massoudi gives repeated-run numbers (N=60).
limits: Web search quota ran out partway; OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar returned 429, so coverage is incomplete. 2024 studies on GPT-4 concept generation not checked.
agent_relevance: Our agent has almost no direct evidence for decomposing design problems; evidence is borrowed from coding and QA. Treat O3 as [S], test first.
